rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a thermal pre-oxidation treatment on Q235 steel to form an iron oxide layer, while the hidden target uses atmospheric plasma spraying to deposit an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on SS316L. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (surface oxidation vs. coating deposition).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses high-humidity air at 25–75 °C, whereas the target uses 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical testing and 900 °C molten-salt hot corrosion. The environments and temperature regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a physical barrier oxide film limiting transport of corrosive species, while the target's mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase hardening, high-entropy sluggish diffusion, and formation of specific Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced corrosion rates (weight loss, pitting, EIS) for pre-oxidized Q235 steel, while the target predicts higher microhardness, better electrochemical polarization resistance, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain for a coated SS316L. The properties and directions are not comparable.
